name: Slow Cooker Greek Chicken Bowls
intro_html: Bright, lemony Greek chicken over tender potatoes is comfort food that doesn't weigh you down. This bowl carries 61 grams of protein for about $3.06 a serving (at everyday cost), and the potato base keeps it hearty and cheap. Fourteen servings out of one pot is a week and a half of no-fuss dinners.
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 8 lb (3450 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast, 8 lb: ~$16.96. Buy 8 lbs: $17.84.
Red Wine Vinegar, 1 tbsp: ~$0.06. Buy 1 (lasts several batches).
Pantry seasonings (dried oregano, salt, onion powder, black pepper): ~$0.33. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $24.05 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.72 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $25.46 across 14 servings, roughly $1.82 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $17.21 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $42.67. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $3.06 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
shop_smart: Potatoes are one of the cheapest fillers going, so buy the ten-pound bag and let it anchor meals all month.
Olive oil looks expensive by the bottle, but a couple tablespoons here costs pennies, so one good bottle stretches for months.
Bottled lime juice works fine and never spoils, so keep it in the fridge door instead of buying fresh citrus you'll forget about.
make_it: Add the chicken, olive oil, lime juice, red wine vinegar, garlic, oregano, onion powder, salt, and pepper to the slow cooker and toss to coat.
Nestle the cut potatoes around and under the chicken so they cook in the juices.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours until the potatoes are fork-tender and the chicken shreds.
Shred the chicken and stir everything together so the potatoes catch the tangy sauce.
Serve the chicken and potatoes together, spooning the pan juices over the top.
portion_html: Each bowl lands at 61 grams of protein and 555 calories, one of the leaner plates in the bunch.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from Rachel Cooks, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
upsell_html: Fresh, filling, and easy on the wallet. Weeknight dinner doesn't get much friendlier. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
